Failed cases retain their IDs and evidence; they are not resampled. A readable pilot remains draft data on native bins. Preparing training labels still requires approved physics/channel conventions and conservative coordinate/grid mapping. 40 focused pilot, reader and Tier A checks pass in full and Tier-A-only modesC-153. Lifecycle checks use fake executables, separately from the saved upstream-file validation. No fresh GENRAY execution or response training is inferred from these tests. The fresh numerical execution is described below, and K-027 remains open.

title: Surrogates
section: EC reference build and original pilot proposal
text:
EC reference build and original pilot proposal
The external reference is built from pinned GENRAY and Giza source archives. Giza provides replacement PGPLOT libraries; compiler and NetCDF paths come from the loaded toolchain. Build configuration overrides the upstream host-specific makefile settings and records optimization, record-marker and legacy argument flags. Sources are unchanged. Cairo/X11 support the plotting dependency. make -j1, one-CPU affinity and a 300-second deadline bound software compilation.
The final build retains the executed helper, source archives, installed plotting libraries, executable and command logs. Every regular artifact has a bound sidecar; source snapshots are roots of an acyclic lineage. Earlier attempts retain their original records and snapshot-lineage limitations. one external reference executable builds with verified artifacts and resolved runtime librariesC-154. Exported plotting symbols and resolved libraries establish link readiness; legacy-source warnings remain. No plotted or scientific output parity is inferred from compilation.
At the original build checkpoint, a separate proposal specified one upstream ITER regression case, one CPU, four GiB, ten minutes of job wall time and a 300-second solver timeout. That proposal preceded owner selection and the failed first execution described below. A content-bound manifest includes case inputs, binary, resolved libraries, toolkit sources, package metadata and job scripts. Its read-only check passes; the launcher refuses changed inputs before execution.
Execution would use a new job-specific directory, immutable binary/input snapshots and the bounded pilot lifecycle described above. The launcher records host, job ID, requested CPU count and actual affinity. Readable output remains draft native-grid data. Review plotting output, process status, profiles and physical integrals before preparing labels; physical thresholds and coordinate, field and signed-current mappings remain owner decisions. K-027 stays open. The historical full-suite statistics remain unchanged.
See entry 32 for this build checkpoint.

title: Surrogates
section: First EC execution and plotting correction
text:
First EC execution and plotting correction
The owner authorized the original ITER numerical pilot and its one-run ceiling. The reference starts, reaches plotting initialization and stops before native NetCDF output. GENRAY requests the PGPLOT /VCPS device; pinned Giza recognizes /CPS and /VPS, but not /VCPS. A failed PGOPEN returns -1. GENRAY’s Fortran STOP branch returns zero, so an exit-code-only check would falsely report success. The pilot runner instead retains output_missing, unchanged input hashes, raw logs, partial outputs and immutable snapshots. No physical channels or integrals are available from this attempt.
The correction is an explicit alias in Giza’s device parser, mapping /VCPS to its existing portrait colour PostScript driver. GENRAY sources and physics inputs remain unchanged. An isolated software build snapshots the patch and executed helper and records hashes; previous builds and the failed run remain immutable. No change is made to the reference physics prescription.
A Fortran probe linked against the original and corrected PGPLOT libraries checks /VPS, /VCPS, /CPS and an invalid device. It uses the real PGOPEN entry point, draws a red line and closes the device. Successful outputs are checked for PostScript headers, page dimensions and colour. The original /VCPS fails; the corrected alias produces portrait output, while an invalid device continues to fail. all eight plotting-device checks match their expected outcomesC-155. This does not establish full GENRAY plotting or scientific parity.
At the correction checkpoint, the exhausted single-run authorization is followed by a fresh bounded retry proposal with unchanged physics inputs and resource ceiling, exact corrected binary/runtime hashes and a passing read-only manifest check. The separately authorized retry is recorded below. Production EC launch/current conventions, conservative radial mapping, physical thresholds and ITER boundary contracts remain open. K-027 and M3 remain open; historical suite statistics are unchanged.
See entry 33 for the failed attempt.

title: Surrogates
text:
Corrected EC numerical pilot
The owner approved one corrected run using the same original ITER input deck, equilibrium, solver source and bounded allocation. Manifest hashes pass before submission. The solver reaches its normal end with readable native output, unchanged input hashes, one-CPU affinity and empty stderr. The raw NetCDF, input/binary snapshots, logs, partial auxiliary files and scheduler records remain immutable and content-bound. the corrected EC reference completes in 83.16 s with readable native profilesC-156.
The output identifies a newer producer than the saved upstream fixture. Native faces, bin volumes and areas match exactly. Power channels are volume-integrated against their matching stored totals; toroidal current is area-integrated against GA_tor_cur_total. Other signed current definitions remain separate. The native ray-stop code records the input remaining-power cutoff, rather than an imposed physical acceptance rule.
The saved-reference comparison records signed total differences and relative weighted L1 profile differences. Power uses native volume weights. Current shape diagnostics use native area weights without claiming that each current definition has that physical integral convention. A zero reference channel has no defined relative error; its absolute difference is retained. Native profiles are not interpolated, clipped, rescaled or converted into a full-LCFS toolkit source. No parity threshold is installed from this one-case comparison.
PostScript opens/closes without Giza errors and renders successfully, but its single page is blank. The magnetic/profile and dispersion plotting switches in the deck are off. This establishes device initialization and format readability, not plotted content or PGPLOT parity. A separate PNG/PDF comparison generated from NetCDF shows overlapping heating/current curves at the displayed scale; negative parallel and positive ONETWO/toroidal signs are retained.
The numerical pilot is complete. Production launch and absorbed-power choices, electron damping channels, ONETWO B_0/sign conversion, conservative grid mapping, fallbacks and rejection criteria remain open before labels can be prepared. Group scope and a new labelling budget must be reviewed separately; the measured one-case runtime does not establish a sampling-domain cost. No production dataset, training, TORAX coupling or response speed-up is claimed. K-027 and M3 remain open; historical suite counts retain their original execution reports.

Native profile comparison






Figure 4: Fresh and saved electron heating, toroidal current and parallel current on the native reference bins. Solid accent lines: corrected pilot; dashed grey lines: older upstream saved output. The curves overlap at this scale. Current signs remain explicit; no full-boundary mapping or physical acceptance is implied.

title: Surrogates
text:
EC label conventions
Purpose. Fix how GENRAY’s native output becomes training labels and, later, TORAX source terms (OQ-21, owner decision 10 Oct 2026). Brief invariants served: units and coordinates explicit, Tier A fallback for every surrogate.
Current drive. The upstream ITER deck’s adjoint calculation (ieffic=6, i_adj=1). The momentum-conserving Lin-Liu calculation (ieffic=4, ieffic_mom_cons=1) runs on a sample of cases as a check, from the upstream variant deck with the same state and launch.
Heating. Electron heating is the sum of GENRAY’s wave-particle (powden_e) and collisional (powden_cl) channels; both are stored separately.
Current. GENRAY’s s_cur_den_onetwo is
\[
j_{12} = \frac{\langle j_\parallel B \rangle}{B_0}, \qquad
j_{12} = j_\parallel \frac{\langle B^2 \rangle}{\langle B \rangle B_0},
\]
the second form being how GENRAY computes it (prep3d.f), with \(B_0\) the vacuum toroidal field bcentr at rcentr in the equilibrium file. TORAX’s EC current input is \(\langle j \cdot B \rangle\) with \(B_0\) also the vacuum field at the major radius, so at coupling \(\langle j \cdot B \rangle = j_{12}\, B_0^{\mathrm{TORAX}}\). The label is multiplied by \(\operatorname{sign}(I_p\, B_0)\) of the equilibrium, so that current along the plasma current is positive.
Radial mapping. GENRAY’s radius (indexrho=2) is \(\sqrt{\Phi/\Phi_s}\) with \(\Phi_s\) the toroidal flux at the reduced boundary psifactr. With \(\Phi(\psi_N) = \int_0^{\psi_N} q\, d\psi_N'\) from the equilibrium’s \(q\) profile,
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \rho_{\mathrm{GENRAY}} \sqrt{\Phi(\psi_{\mathrm{factr}})/\Phi(1)} .
\]
Heating and current are remapped onto uniform output cells by interpolating the cumulative integrals \(\int p\, dV\) and \(\int j_{12}\, dA\) (GENRAY’s own bin volumes and areas) at the output faces and differencing. The integral over every output cell equals GENRAY’s; cells beyond GENRAY’s last face receive zero. The current’s area integral is GENRAY’s GA_tor_cur_total.
Power. 170 GHz, O-mode, one central ray as in the deck; labels are divided by the injected power and stored per MW. Linear scaling with power is assumed in use.
Fallback. The Gaussian EC model with centre, width and current-drive efficiency fitted to the labels. Acceptance. Set by the owner after the baseline (B3).

title: Surrogates
text:
ITER pedestal conversion
Purpose. Turn the selected EPEDNN network’s outputs into TORAX’s prescribed-pedestal fields (OQ-21, owner decision 10 Oct 2026).
Method. For EPEDNN inputs \(x\) (upstream order and units, \(n_{e,\mathrm{ped}}\) in \(10^{19}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\)):

Branch: both diamagnetic corrections (GH), solution 0, which is upstream’s GH.H, the H-mode branch and the upstream default.
Temperatures: \(T_i = T_e = T\) at the pedestal top, with \(p = n_e (1 + n_\mathrm{ions}/n_e)\, T\). For main ions of charge \(Z_m\) and one impurity of charge \(Z\), \(n_\mathrm{ions}/n_e = \frac{Z - Z_\mathrm{eff}}{Z_m (Z - Z_m)} + \frac{Z_\mathrm{eff} - Z_m}{Z (Z - Z_m)}\).
Density: the prescribed \(n_{e,\mathrm{ped}}\), which is also the network’s input.
Pedestal top: \(\psi_N = 1 - 2w\), with \(w\) the network’s width, documented upstream as the half width in normalised poloidal flux, mapped to \(\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\) through the equilibrium’s monotone \(\psi_N(\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}})\).
Fallback: the prescribed pedestal wherever the input-box check fails, an output is not finite, \(T \le 0\), or the top falls outside \((0, 1)\).

Pure JAX; the selection uses where, so the function compiles once and has finite gradients inside the box. On the upstream ITER example: pedestal pressure 0.0772 MPa, T_ped 3.59 keV at n_e,ped 7e19 m^-3, top at psi_norm 0.935C-162.
Correctness. 19 focused checks (13 EC pipeline, 6 pedestal contract) pass in full and Tier-A-only modesC-163. The pedestal tests compare the branch with the raw output vector, the ion fraction with its pure-hydrogen and pure-impurity limits, the temperature and top mapping with hand calculations, the fallback with out-of-box inputs, and JIT and gradient inside the box. The network’s physics is used as selected and not tested here.
Not yet done. Coupling into TORAX (B5); MAST-U keeps its prescribed pedestal.

title: Surrogates
text:
EC dataset v1
Purpose. Reference labels for the EC surrogate on ITER states the coupling loop visits (OQ-21 scope B, owner decision 10 Oct 2026). Plan: configs/sampling/m3_genray_ec_v1.yaml; producer tkit.datasets.genray_ec; job scripts/m3_genray_ec.sbatch.
Algorithm.

States. The 39 ITER TORAX runs of the dataset-v3 family (M1 benchmark case, ITER hybrid flat top and ITER ramp-up, with heating and density scaled) are run again, keeping \(T_e\), \(n_e\) and \(Z_\mathrm{eff}\) over time. Eight states per run, evenly spaced in time after the first tenth of the run.
Deck. Each state’s profiles are interpolated onto GENRAY’s 21-point tabular grid (uniform in GENRAY’s radius, converted as in EC label conventions) and written into the upstream deck’s density, temperature and \(Z_\mathrm{eff}\) tables. Nothing else in the deck changes except the launch.
Launch. Ten launches per state, five per family. Equatorial launcher: the deck’s own launch point, polar and toroidal angles drawn uniformly around the deck’s direction on its co-current side. Upper launcher: an approximate public position (from the published ITER EC code benchmark, not an ITER design value), aimed downward with poloidal steering. Angles use the deck’s toray convention.
Run. One GENRAY process per core in a node-local scratch directory, with a timeout. Kept per case: the deck, the output file, compressed console logs and a record with hashes, exit status and wall time. GENRAY’s adjoint scratch files are discarded.
Assemble. Two response datasets with the same inputs (\(T_e\), \(n_e\), \(Z_\mathrm{eff}\) on the 21 points, launcher flag, launch position and angles): case totals (wave-particle and collisional absorbed power, driven current) and profiles on 50 uniform cells in \(\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\). Splits hold out whole TORAX runs. Failed cases would be kept with their status and never fitted; there were none.

Results. 3120 of 3120 cases produce readable output (20 of 20 check cases); median 84.8 s of GENRAY time per caseC-164. Current-drive check: median 4.1% difference in driven current (range -14% to +16%), identical absorbed powerC-165.

Incomplete absorption occurs for cold, dense L-mode states at the largest toroidal angles (single pass). A few upper-launcher cases drive small counter-current at large radius. The collisional channel is zero in every case: the deck does not enable collisional damping. The largest currents come from early ramp-up states traced through the full-current equilibrium (K-028).
Baseline. The existing response trainer with its defaults (five members, two hidden layers of 64), on case totals and, separately, on profiles with \(\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\) as an extra input: driven current RMSE 3.30 kA/MW against 13.5 kA/MW for the training mean; pointwise profile model: current-density RMSE 2.20e4 A/m^2 against 2.09e4 A/m^2 for the meanC-166. The totals are learned; the pointwise profile model is no better than the training mean. B4 needs a structured profile output (centre, width, totals).
Ceilings. K-028: one equilibrium for every state; collisional channel inactive. The upper-launcher position is approximate.

title: Surrogates
text:
Structured EC surrogate
Purpose. The EC surrogate of M3: GENRAY’s absorbed power, driven current and deposition profiles from the plasma state and the launch, behind a guard with the Gaussian EC model as fallback (OQ-21, owner decisions 10 Oct 2026).
Targets (configs/surrogates/m3_ec_targets.yaml), measured once on the test split, whole held-out TORAX runs, per MW injected:








output
metric
limit




absorbed power
median relative error
0.10


driven current (cases above one kiloampere per MW)
median relative error
0.10


heating deposition centre
median absolute error in \(\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\)
0.05



K-028 restriction. States are kept when their prescribed plasma current (from the TORAX configuration, piecewise linear in time) is at least two thirds of the equilibrium’s: 2910 of 3120 cases kept (210 early ramp-up cases dropped); largest driven current 61 kA/MW, was 279 kA/MWC-167. The test split keeps the same eight held-out runs.
Labels. Six numbers per case from GENRAY’s native bins: absorbed electron power \(P\), co-current driven current \(I\), and for heating and for current the centre \(c\) and width \(w\),
\[
c = \frac{\sum_k \rho_k\, q_k}{\sum_k q_k}, \qquad
w^2 = \frac{\sum_k (\rho_k - c)^2\, q_k}{\sum_k q_k},
\]
with \(q_k = p_k V_k\) for heating (power density times bin volume) and \(q_k = |j_{12,k}| A_k\) for current (bin area), \(\rho_k\) in \(\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\).
Model. The existing response ensemble (five members) on the 68 inputs of EC dataset v1. Four sizes (width 64 or 128, depth 2 or 3) were trained; all pass on validation, and the width-128, depth-3 model is best on every validation metric. Outputs are bounded before use: absorbed power between zero and the injected power, centres in \([0, 1]\), widths at least \(10^{-3}\).
Profiles. The heating (or current) density in cell \(i\) between faces \(\rho_{i}\) and \(\rho_{i+1}\) is
\[
p_i = \frac{P\, f_i}{V_i}, \qquad
f_i = \frac{\Phi\big(\frac{\rho_{i+1}-c}{w}\big) - \Phi\big(\frac{\rho_i-c}{w}\big)}
{\Phi\big(\frac{1-c}{w}\big) - \Phi\big(\frac{-c}{w}\big)},
\]
with \(\Phi\) the standard normal distribution function and \(V_i\) the cell volume (area for current). The integral of the profile equals the predicted total exactly, also when the width is below one cell, which is the case for about half the labels.
Results. all three targets pass: absorbed power 0.01% and driven current 2.7% median relative error (targets 10%), heating centre 0.0036 median absolute error in rho (target 0.05)C-168. Profiles: heating RMSE 8.6e3 W/m^3 (training mean 1.34e4, Gaussian of the true parameters 5.4e3); current RMSE 1.35e4 A/m^2 (training mean 2.09e4, Gaussian of the true parameters 5.0e3)C-169.
Correctness. 19 focused checks (15 EC pipeline and structured labels, 4 structured evaluation) pass in full and Tier-A-only modesC-170. The tests check the current interpolation, the moments and sign of the structured labels on a synthetic output, the output bounds, the masking and pass/fail logic of the target scoring, and conservation and centring of the cell-integrated Gaussian for a narrow and a wide deposition.
Ceilings. K-028 (narrowed, still open); one central ray per case; spread not calibrated.
Reproducing. python -m tkit.datasets.genray_ec structured; python -m tkit.surrogates.responses ec-genray-iter-v1-structured.npz <out> --config configs/surrogates/m3_ec_structured_w128d3.json --allow-draft; python -m tkit.surrogates.ec_structured <out> --split test. Entry: 38.

title: Verification
text:
Checked exports
tkit.verify.export makes fixed float64 PyTorch copies of the Equinox networks. It includes input transforms, normalization and physical output transforms. Transport’s served response averages members in training space before inverse signed-log; EC clamps the raw mean after averaging. The selected pedestal retains its power-law residual, tanh-GELU, squared outputs and density scaling, with every solution explicit.
check_parity rejects nonfinite arrays, shape differences and a discrepancy beyond the selected numeric criterion. OQ-26 approves mixed relative and absolute parity after the relative-only check exposed cancellation near zero: 13 export checks pass in each mode: all selected members, random box points, local holdouts, physical transforms and served means, with rtol=1e-12 and atol=1e-12 in each declared output unitC-180. Formal proofs may not bypass this gate. The artifact manifests bind model, metadata and explicit box files and allow transport exports to load without opening the large training datasets. They establish storage consistency, not proved physical behavior (OQ-23).

title: Verification

Property contracts
six property contracts load; 14 property-validation tests pass in each mode, including malformed-domain, tolerance and output-schema rejectionC-177. tkit.verify.properties validates model scopes, output names, finite ordered boxes, the declared box data source, robustness tolerances and owner decisions. The existing OQ-20 monotonicity contract is retained.
The formal engine is auto_LiRPA with the input-splitting loop described below, under OQ-24. Bounds target every member; local robustness targets the served ensemble response. Launcher families stay categorical, and complete perturbation boxes that leave a training domain will be reported separately. No training box is silently shrunk to make a property pass.

title: Verification
text:
Closed-loop comparison
tkit.verify.closed_loop reads provenance-bound saved runs and rejects unmatched settings, time/radial grids, nonfinite profiles or unconverged solver records. It checks that a face served by the surrogate was served by TGLF in the reference.
The historical paper eq. 41 convention is retained:
\[ E = 100\frac{\sqrt{\operatorname{mean}((T_{sur}-T_{ref})^2)}}
                    {\operatorname{mean}(T_{sur})}. \]
The guard is defined on faces, while temperatures are cell-centred. Both temperatures are linearly interpolated to the same served faces. Whole-profile errors and a supplementary comparison using cells with both adjacent faces served remain visible. The saved runs’ grids are uniform; the reader rejects other grids without explicit face coordinates.
ITER passes (served-face T_e 7.42%, T_i 8.18%, both passing the 15% limit; whole profile 7.72/9.23%; 34 of 51 final-state faces servedC-178). MAST-U fails (served-face T_e 35.33%, T_i 49.15%, both failing 15%; whole profile 41.51/62.39%; cells with both adjacent faces served give 11.86/23.24%, still failing T_i; 13 of 26 final-state faces servedC-179), with the conservative cell diagnostic also failing ion temperature. Its failure remains ceiling K-030. The mask is only the final accepted state’s guard diagnostic; it does not measure fallback calls throughout the trajectory.

MAST-U scope (OQ-42)
Decided 25 Oct 2026. The MAST-U comparison against a TGLF reference trajectory (remediation step R6) is recorded as not evaluable, and MAST-U is certified at the M4 review with that limitation stated, alongside K-030 and K-032. title: Verification

MAST-U remediation diagnosis
The owner prioritizes the failed MAST-U criterion (OQ-25). Matched final-state probes show substantial flux error: all 17 in-domain final-state probes succeed; on 12 served faces with reference flux above 1 gB, median relative errors are 41.17% Q_e and 74.27% Q_i; an unconstrained v3 control gives 38.05/71.88%C-181. The existing unconstrained v3 model also misses those feedback states. That control is diagnostic and does not meet the owner’s monotonicity contract; pointwise scores are not a coupled comparison.
The accepted-state replay reproduces the failed saved trajectory: all saved temperature, density and psi values are reproduced exactly; four final inner faces exceed the existing ion-diffusivity guard bound; 44.81% of accepted-state face diagnostics reject the surrogateC-182. Four final inner faces lie in the model’s box but exceed the ion-diffusivity guard bound. Captured masks cover accepted states, not the solver’s intermediate evaluations. The isolated inner served face has zero final heat flux in both model and TGLF even though its temperature differs. No face is removed from the acceptance comparison.
The approved refresh collected feedback-state labels on training equilibria only, with both test equilibria excluded. It retains full solver inputs and applies the approved-region filter. The local result review checks the finished artifacts: eight local checks pass for approved allocation/time, hashes and lineage, full-input alignment, case budget, unique coordinates, training-only equilibria, source model and finite successful labelsC-183. It compares each label input row with the selected case and the source trajectory’s accepted-state solver arrays, and binds lineage by hash. These checks establish collection integrity; they do not establish held-out accuracy or a successful coupled remedy. The owner approved artifact synchronization in OQ-28. We checked remote privacy settings and downloaded every uploaded record by artifact identifier: all 26 uploaded artifact records covering 18 distinct files match both remote SHA-256 metadata and downloaded bytes; the folder and private visibility match the approved request, and the offline payload queue is emptyC-184. Duplicate provenance sidecars are retained as distinct records; name-based retrieval is ambiguous for those duplicates. title: Verification
text:
Candidate replay preparation
Entry 48 records R6 tooling. The runner supports an explicit immutable candidate directory while preserving default model selection. New trajectories record the full scenario configuration, source runner, model and metadata, scenario plan and equilibrium provenance. Preparation binds a source snapshot and checks every external input digest and environment version before execution.
Reference reuse reconstructs the historical scenario from its checksum-bound runner and clean source revision. Physics/core/dataset modules and the scenario plan are byte-identical to that revision. Solver, fallback, wrapper post-processing and guard settings match recorded metadata; the candidate differs in its model path. Its previously audited box stays fixed. Historical metadata lacks the run index, but its bound runner selects the first scenario explicitly. External dependency bytes and a full resolved configuration were not recorded historically; the audit states that limitation and checks pinned/current versions instead of supplying retrospective hashes. Actual post-run configuration, grids, time points, provenance and finite convergence remain required.
The formal comparison uses every candidate-served face, interpolating both profiles onto those coordinates and normalizing RMS difference by the candidate temperature mean. The report retains original served-mask counts, overlap and faces added/removed. A separate fixed-baseline-mask diagnostic evaluates the candidate temperatures on the old faces; it never replaces the formal mask. Whole-profile and both-adjacent-faces cell errors are retained. An isolated served face remains eligible for the formal metric even when the supplementary cell metric is unavailable. Existing comparison defaults are preserved.
Accepted-state history captures generic guard features and raw coefficients before post-processing. Rejection diagnostics count model-domain violations, generic feature finiteness/box failures, nonfinite coefficients, negative diffusivities, excessive diffusivity and convection. Predicate counts overlap, so a separate priority partition provides counts that sum to the number of rejected face states. Candidate diagnostics must reproduce the saved raw predicate exactly. The historical replay lacks generic features; its unavailable predicate evidence stays explicit. These rates describe accepted states, not intermediate transport calls, and no fallback acceptance threshold is chosen.
40 focused checks pass in normal and Tier A modes; the two-step training-only candidate smoke is finite and reconstructs the raw accepted-state guard predicate exactlyC-188 checks configuration/mask isolation, raw guard accounting, immutable package/input rejection and historical runner compatibility. A bounded two-step smoke uses a training equilibrium only and validates source-package execution, finite profiles and raw guard reconstruction. Saved baseline artifacts also reproduce the existing comparison exactly through the new report. No held-out candidate result or formal certificate is claimed.

title: Verification
text:

title: The EC and ITER pedestal surrogates inside TORAX
text:
new component Entry 39 · milestone M3

M3 requires each surrogate to run inside the coupling loop, to be differentiable there, and to have its cost measured. The structured electron-cyclotron (EC) surrogate (entry 38) and the ITER pedestal network (entry 36) existed only as standalone models. The Primer explains sources and the pedestal; terms are in the Glossary.
EC. TORAX’s EC source already returns both a heating profile and a driven-current profile, so the surrogate is registered as a new model of that source rather than as a new channel. At each step it reads the electron temperature, density and effective charge from TORAX’s state, evaluates the ensemble, and rebuilds the two profiles on TORAX’s own cells so that their integrals equal the predicted totals. A guard decides for the whole profile: if the inputs leave the training box or the ensemble members disagree too much, TORAX’s Gaussian EC model with parameters fitted to the GENRAY labels is used instead. A first version rebuilt the model function on every run, so TORAX recompiled each time; it is now cached.
Pedestal. The network is registered as a TORAX pedestal model whose prescribed values are the fallback. Its ten inputs come from TORAX’s geometry and profiles, including the normalised beta computed by TORAX. One input needed a convention: EPED takes the ion mass number (2.5 for deuterium-tritium), while TORAX holds the mass in atomic units, slightly above the network’s training range. With the mass number, the network sets the pedestal on every state.
Checks. On the ITER hybrid scenario, with part of the scenario’s generic heating moved to EC at the same total power, both models run in TORAX’s compiled step with the Newton solver, close the discrete energy and particle balance, and have derivatives through the solver that agree with finite differences (runs under jit for both launchers with the surrogate serving the source; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7C-171; runs under jit with EPEDNN setting the pedestal; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7C-173). These checks compare the coupled code with itself under perturbation; they do not test the physics of either reference.



quantity
result




EC over the full trajectory
surrogate serves 29 of 30 states (upper launcher) and 16 of 27 (equatorial; core T_e leaves the training range); run time 1.6-1.7 times the analytic source; one call 39 microseconds against 85 s for GENRAYC-172


pedestal over the full trajectory
EPEDNN sets the pedestal on 48 of 48 states: T_ped 2.62-2.69 keV, top 0.90-0.92; final stored thermal energy 220 MJ against 303 MJ, beta_N 1.57 against 2.16; about 1.5 times the prescribed model per stepC-174



With central EC deposition the core temperature rises past the largest value in the EC training data, and the guard hands over to the fallback for the rest of that run. The upper launcher deposits off-axis and the surrogate serves almost every state. The network’s pedestal is lower than the scenario’s prescribed one, and stored energy and normalised beta fall with it; normalised beta is also an input to the network, so the loop settles on a consistent value.
All four M3 surrogates (transport per machine, EC, ITER pedestal) now run inside TORAX. The remaining question for M3 is in the next entry.

title: The MAST-U transport surrogate in the loop, and the M3 acceptance audit
text:
measurement negative result Entry 40 · milestone M3

Before auditing M3 we listed, for each surrogate, the evidence for the three acceptance criteria: held-out accuracy, running differentiably inside the loop, and measured speed-up. One gap appeared. The in-loop checks of the transport surrogate had all used the ITER ensemble; the MAST-U ensemble had been scored on held-out data but never run inside TORAX. The Primer explains the loop; terms are in the Glossary.
MAST-U in the loop. We took MAST-U states from transport dataset v3, with their FreeGSNKE equilibria, and replaced the runs’ Bohm/gyro-Bohm transport with the guarded MAST-U surrogate. With the runs’ own linear solver every step converges and the guard hands the faces outside the training window to the fallback. With the Newton solver the result is partly negative: from these initial states Newton does not reach TORAX’s tolerance at the runs’ time step, and reaches it at small steps only for some equilibria. The initial states are not in equilibrium; even the native transport changes the core temperature quickly. We recorded this as ceiling K-029 and did not loosen the tolerance. On a case where Newton converges, energy balance closes and derivatives through the solver agree with finite differences (linear solver: every step converges on two equilibria with the fallback serving 31-35% of faces; on a converging Newton case energy balance within 1e-6 and derivatives match finite differences to 1e-7; Newton does not converge at the runs’ 5 ms steps from these initial states (K-029)C-175).

title: M3 closed: surrogates for transport, EC heating and the ITER pedestal
text:
measurement decision Entry 41 · milestone M3

M3 built fast surrogates for the expensive physics and ran them inside the coupling loop. Its three acceptance criteria are held-out accuracy, differentiable execution inside the loop, and a measured end-to-end speed-up. The audit in entry 40 left one measurement open: MAST-U transport timed against TGLF inside TORAX. The owner approved one compute-node job for it. The M3 page has the full record.
A failed first run. The job stopped after a minute. TORAX’s preparation of TGLF inputs gives the two radial points nearest the magnetic axis meaningless values on the MAST-U geometry, a safety factor of order ten to the seventeenth among them. TGLF’s eigensolver fails on these and TGLF ends its worker process, which ends the whole TORAX run. We reproduced it point by point on a login node. Such points are now not sent to TGLF; they receive no value and the guard serves them from the fallback, the same treatment the surrogate gets outside its training box. The owner approved the same job again.
MAST-U result. TGLF 364.1 s, surrogate 0.492 s, Bohm/gyro-Bohm 0.043 s: the surrogate is about 740 times faster than TGLF; profile deviation from TGLF at 0.2 s, T_e 41.5% and T_i 62.4% (Bohm/gyro-Bohm 47.9% and 84.6%), with half the faces outside the training window and on the fallbackC-176. The speed-up is of the same order as on ITER (TGLF 539.1 s, final v3 surrogate 1.249 s, QLKNN 0.117 s; the v3 surrogate is about 432 times faster than TGLF and 10.7 times slower than QLKNNC-158). The profile agreement is much weaker than on ITER: at the final time half the radial points of this MAST-U run lie outside the surrogate’s training window, and the fallback serves them. Where the surrogate serves, the profiles stay closer to TGLF than the fallback’s. This is the domain limitation the brief asks to report rather than hide; it is carried into M4 as a stated limit.

title: The MAST-U candidate replay fails reference coverage
text:
measurement Entry 49 · milestone M4

The owner approved the prepared local replay once. The solver completed with finite, converged profiles, but the comparison stopped because a face served by the candidate used fallback in the saved physics reference: the single approved replay finishes in 65 seconds within its 240-second bound, with 40 finite converged steps and 146 passing integrity checks; comparison exits with a reference-coverage failure at candidate-served face 4, normalized radius 0.16C-189.
That reference cannot establish the formal temperature criterion for this candidate. The failing face stays in its actual served mask. We neither intersect masks nor substitute the historical baseline mask for acceptance. The saved trajectory, source snapshot, provenance and failure logs remain available; no solver retry was made.
The supplementary comparisons retain mixed results: candidate/baseline serve 15/13 faces with 11 overlapping; fixed-baseline-mask candidate T_e/T_i errors are 42.1252%/48.1182%, versus baseline 35.3331%/49.1458%; candidate whole-profile errors are 29.7365%/41.8856%, and own-mask descriptive distances to the hybrid reference are 29.8865%/40.0063%C-190. Electron temperature worsens on the fixed baseline mask. Smaller whole-profile errors and lower descriptive distances on the candidate’s own faces do not establish improved coupled accuracy. Those own-mask distances compare against a trajectory containing fallback at the uncovered face and are explicitly ineligible for acceptance.
Raw guard reconstruction matches every saved accepted-state face. Rejections decrease: candidate rejects 415/1040 accepted-state face records (39.9038%), versus baseline 466/1040 (44.8077%); exclusive candidate reasons are 341 model-box exits, 50 excessive diffusivities and 24 excessive convection values, with exact raw guard reconstructionC-191. This is accepted-state accounting; it does not measure intermediate solver calls, and the owner has not set a fallback-rate acceptance threshold.
The historical reference lacks raw rejection reasons. Repeating identical reference compute would not establish that the missing face becomes admissible. Its cause and a physically justified remedy need review before a new reference request. A separate sampling experiment can also be prepared from training-only evidence, with original holdouts and the physical contract preserved. Neither experiment has been authorized.
K-030 remains open. The current model and guard stay selected, and nothing has been synchronized or replaced.
What’s next. Review the reference-coverage failure and bounded follow-up proposal before new training or coupled compute. Formal certification remains unfinished.

title: Surrogates
Surrogates
text:
ITER pedestal in TORAX
Method. tkit_epednn, a TORAX pedestal model derived from set_T_ped_n_ped, whose prescribed fields are the fallback. Inputs per step: minor radius, \(\beta_N\) (TORAX’s definition), \(B_0\), triangularity and elongation of the last face, \(I_p\), the main-ion mass number, the prescribed \(n_{e,\mathrm{ped}}\), major radius and \(Z_\mathrm{eff}\) at the prescribed top. The conversion is the pedestal contract, with \(n_\mathrm{ions}/n_e\) from TORAX’s main-ion and impurity densities and \(\psi_N(\rho)\) from TORAX’s current \(\psi\). Fallback outside the input box, for non-finite outputs, or for \(T_\mathrm{ped}\) outside 0.5-15 keV or a top outside 0.75-0.99.
Mass number, deliberately. EPED’s m is the main-ion mass number (2.5 for 50:50 D-T in the upstream ITER example); TORAX’s A_i is the mass in amu (2.515), which lies outside the network’s training range. The model uses the fraction-weighted mass number of the configured main ions.
Correctness. runs under jit with EPEDNN setting the pedestal; energy balance within 1e-6 and particles within 1e-10; derivatives through Newton match finite differences to 1e-7C-173. Trajectory and cost. EPEDNN sets the pedestal on 48 of 48 states: T_ped 2.62-2.69 keV, top 0.90-0.92; final stored thermal energy 220 MJ against 303 MJ, beta_N 1.57 against 2.16; about 1.5 times the prescribed model per stepC-174.

title: Surrogates
text:
M4 feedback retraining preparation
Entry 46 records the preparation. An optional extra-dataset path mapping resolves repository-relative or absolute sources; without it, previous dataset paths and deterministic splits are unchanged. The feedback source explicitly has zero holdout. Every retained row carries an index into its immutable source, and feedback rows also retain run, equilibrium, accepted step and face coordinates.
The frozen manifest binds the recipe, baseline model, source and sidecar hashes, and a compressed artifact containing successful-row indices and all split indices. Held-out sources appear separately from training sources. Exact row hashes compare model features and all solver inputs shared between source schemas. A cross-split match blocks fitting until investigation; this audit found none. Full feedback inputs are also checked against case records and their provenance-bound accepted-state trajectories.
The existing feature builder, monotone heads, signed-log outputs, clipping, stability penalty and optimizer recipe are retained. Input and target normalization are recomputed using augmented training rows only, with differences from the baseline recorded. All feedback rows lie inside the existing physical box, so its endpoints remain unchanged.
The bounded smoke selects rows only from original training indices and the training-only feedback source. Its checkpoint fixture is drawn from original training rows; no feedback row is held out. Evaluation source files are not opened. Source snapshots, finite predictions, normalization, timings and exact checkpoint reload are recorded. Checks: 55 focused checks pass in both normal and Tier A modes; the bounded training-only smoke produces finite predictions and reloads exactlyC-185. No smoke accuracy is reported as acceptance evidence.
Production fitting rejects changes to the frozen recipe, sources, indices or domain. A dedicated batch executes hashed source snapshots and retains selected per-member epochs, training/validation history, actual per-source minibatch counts and provenance for every source. Pooled permutations still drop incomplete final batches; recording sampled counts does not add loss weighting or duplicate feedback rows. The source package includes the batch script, configuration and frozen split/manifest artifacts. Its reviewed hash is required at execution. Approval, production training, offline acceptance, coupled revalidation and replacement remain separate stages.

section: M4 feedback candidate completion and offline review
text:
M4 feedback candidate completion and offline review
Entry 47 records the approved candidate’s completion. The job records native scheduler allocation and final accounting, process exit, executed batch and the reviewed package digest. A separate completion audit checks every hashed snapshot file, model/metadata provenance, original source and split identities, checkpoint epochs, history, actual sampling counts and read-only model files (164 completion checks pass, binding the saved candidate to the reviewed snapshot and frozen data/splits, with finite parameters/history and tested member/served predictionsC-186). Training-only normalization agrees with the frozen preparation at mixed relative/absolute tolerance \(10^{-12}\), and the physical box is unchanged.
The offline comparison reads the saved post-fit metrics for frozen validation and original holdouts, retaining the metadata hashes and common scoring recipe. It checks that source hashes, seed, split rules, population sizes and reference-floor counts match the baseline. The full designated test population is kept. Refresh scores are recomputed on every valid refresh row and labelled training scores. Paired reports retain median and tail errors, coverage, stability and clipping behavior, including regressions. The held-out flux gate passes for each channel, with mixed changes relative to the baseline; refresh medians improve modestly while tails worsen. These observations do not select a new seed or recipe.
Parity uses the same physical inputs for JAX and float64 PyTorch. Each member is compared in signed-log training and physical flux units; the served ensemble is compared after the training-space mean and inverse transform. Points comprise seeded random-box inputs, frozen original test inputs, refresh training inputs and the lower/upper corners and centre. JAX JIT/eager comparisons are included. All comparison records meet OQ-26’s \(|\Delta y| \le 10^{-12} + 10^{-12}|y_{\mathrm{JAX}}|\) (all 168 export comparison records pass the unchanged mixed tolerance, covering all 20 members in training/physical units, the served ensemble and JAX JIT/eager arithmeticC-187). Relative-only failures and maximum absolute discrepancies remain in the audit so that the mixed decision is reproducible.
Saved-parameter diagnostics verify paired gradients are absent from the free trunk, positive affine scales, matching output/input pairs and finite effective absolute weights. JAX directional derivatives of the actual physical member and served paths include preprocessing, affine normalization, output clipping and inverse signed-log. No sampled required-pair slope is negative. Those diagnostics are finite checks and architecture inspections; the formal M4 proof remains pending.
The candidate is not selected by the default guard. Its matched coupled replay remains a separate next step, with existing temperature limits and guard settings. K-030 remains open, and any future synchronization is reviewed against its actual payload.

title: Verification
text:
Signed heat conversion review
The saved-state review reconstructs face temperatures and radial derivatives with the pinned transport solver’s cell representation and bound magnetic geometry. Source checks cover the recorded conversion, geometry and gradient files. No simulation or transport model is prepared; physical solver calls are forbidden. Every state of the investigated face is retained.
For each heat channel the converter uses
[ P_s=Q_s^{gB}Q_{GB},V’/_b, s=-P_s/(n_s{_n}T_s,g_1/V’+), ]
with temperature in joules and the fixed numerical denominator correction. Inverting this equation gives an inferred heat flux, which is converted back through the native implementation. 33 focused checks pass in each mode, including 14 new sign/units/history tests; all 80 native heat-converter round trips meet the mixed 1e-12 parity criterion (maximum absolute difference 8.88e-16 m²/s), 32 numerical source files match the diagnostic bindings, and all 78 source modules pass typingC-196 records those numerical checks and synthetic tests. A round trip checks algebra and units; it cannot independently validate the originating solver flux.
the final electron heat flux is inferred as -0.001689376033 gB; all 9 negative channel records at 8 accepted states have outward-decreasing temperature and no denominator-epsilon sign reversal, with maximum epsilon ratio 1.03e-11; all negative magnitudes are below 1 gBC-195 narrows the sign diagnosis. Temperatures decrease outward in all negative heat-channel records, and the denominator correction changes none of their signs. The saved coefficients therefore imply inward signed heat flux in this representation. Their magnitudes are below the offline accuracy gate’s reference-flux floor; neither that gate nor their small size establishes physical validity or a numerical-error explanation. The inferred ion channel is the reference worker’s sum over main and impurity ions, whereas the surrogate learns main-ion heat flux. Separate species contributions remain unobserved.
The current raw guard rejects negative diffusivity before post-processing. Moving a positive floor before that rejection changes reference physics and coverage. A signed-flux-preserving closure would require an explicit stable representation and compatible surrogate contract; it cannot be inferred from one effective coefficient. The current in-memory interface does not expose mode spectra, so richer collection requires another prepared output route.
This is an algebraic/source review, not an adopted physical remedy. OQ-32 now selects retaining the current nonnegative contract while investigating. Formal candidate acceptance remains not evaluable, and K-030 stays open. Current model/guard, every face, splits and tolerances are preserved. Draft entry 52 is held for private owner review.

title: Verification
text:
Owner disposition and licence
The owner selected retaining the existing positive-flux approximation, physical contract and raw guard (OQ-32). Richer direct-flux and supported mode evidence requires a prepared diagnostic output route, validated tooling and a concrete execution review. The existing inferred-flux and conversion evidence remains qualified as in C-195/C-196; this decision supplies no new physics measurement and makes no rejected face admissible.
OQ-17 selects MIT for original toolkit code/documentation. The root licence has copyright 2026 Vignesh Gopakumar; package metadata reads the licence file. Local source and wheel builds contain that text and declare the licence file. The wheel retains the existing EPEDNN licence and notice byte-for-byte. These packaging checks do not replace dependency/data redistribution reviews or authorize a public release. Runtime source, tests and model selection are unchanged; the retained test statistics remain historical execution evidence.

title: Verification
text:
Direct heat diagnostic route
An original native driver links the byte-bound TGLF library, reads the complete generated input and executes one local-state solve. Full-precision text retains particle and heat flux by species, low-k heat totals, the native ky grid and weights, growth/frequency pairs, and saturated and quasilinear heat spectra by species, field, ky and mode. An independent synthetic branch fills those arrays without reading an equilibrium or calling the solver. The strict reader rejects missing, extra, nonfinite or dimensionally inconsistent records.
The paired route runs the pinned in-memory wrapper in a fresh process with the same complete defaults, global settings and prepared local inputs. Input precedence matches the reference worker. Native shape parameter names omit the wrapper’s local suffix; mapping them preserves register values and the native generated-file audit checks all settings. No parser default silently replaces a declared value.
For the declared logarithmic ky grid, each interval uses D = log(k1/k0)/(k1-k0), w1 = k1*(1-k0*D) and w0 = k0*(k1*D-1), with first weights zero and the first ky. The contribution is w0*previous_spectrum + w1*current_spectrum. Sum all fields, modes and intervals for total heat; native low-k heat retains phi and perpendicular magnetic fields through ky at most one. Keep all signed contributions and compare totals at mixed relative/absolute tolerance 1e-12 in gyro-Bohm units.
Separate comparisons report native versus paired species fluxes, and paired electron/total-ion flux versus the saved inverse conversion. Any disagreement is retained as diagnostic evidence. The native sheared double-pass eigenvalues may retain unsheared first-pass values; growth/frequency pairs alone neither label a mode physically nor prove numerical convergence. Solver status and finite output checks supply only the supported numerical diagnostics.
55 focused checks pass in each mode, including 22 direct-output and settings checks; all 79 source modules pass typing; the compiled synthetic writer preserves signed species heat and passes total/low-k spectral parity without calling TGLFC-197 records preparation checks. This does not establish direct physical flux parity, reference admissibility or coupled acceptance. OQ-33’s permission for runs shorter than six hours leaves the selected model/guard, physical contract, training isolation and owner physics decisions in force.

title: Verification
text:
Diagnostic wrapper status fix
The first rich diagnostic failed in paired reporting after its first solve: the compiled wrapper exposes integrated flux registers but not the Fortran interface’s error-status register. Source availability is insufficient evidence of Python-interface availability. The consumed attempt retains partial native output, failed logs, executed-call count and final scheduler accounting.
Paired reporting now records whether status is exposed, preserves absent status as unavailable, validates finite fluxes and retains any reported failure status. Native status remains available through the driver. This checks software/output integrity; unavailable convergence evidence is not replaced by a zero status. 25 diagnostic checks pass in each mode, including unavailable status, exposed failure status and nonfinite output; 33 unchanged focused checks are retained for 58 focused recorded passes per modeC-198 binds the synthetic worker regressions. A new package is frozen after the correction, with a separate summary and retained test-report directory; consumed request evidence is never overwritten. ## Signed reference literature review {#signed-reference-literature-review}
The complete local-state collection is retained despite a subsequent tracking failure (648 integrity checks pass on the complete 15-state collection; all affected signed states agree between backends, but four control states fail the existing parity criterion; original terminal tracking failure is preserved and archive recovery calls no solverC-199). The offline tracker copied repeated basenames; archival recovery instead preserves relative case paths in one checksum-bound bundle. Recovery does not call the solver or alter original accounting.
The owner delegates approval of the recommended reference method (OQ-34). The target is signed, species-resolved TGLF with fixed turbulence settings and matched geometry, normalization and transport equations. The present guarded hybrid trajectory remains a regression baseline with unresolved coverage. Numerical reproducibility, physical validation and coupled acceptance are distinct.
GACODE output definitions distinguish species energy weights, eigenvalues and integrated spectra. Staebler et al. (2024), §5.2 motivates checking anomalous reduced-model cases before higher-fidelity gyrokinetic study. Snoep et al. (2025) demonstrates matched spectral and heat-flux verification. Lestz et al. (2025) shows spherical-tokamak predictions depend on turbulence and transport treatment. These sources support the verification method, not this case’s physical validity.
Repeatability tooling retains two fresh-process results per selected state and backend, each compared with its consumed output at the existing mixed 1e-12 criterion (31 synthetic diagnostic tests pass in each mode, including archive identity and repeatability completeness/discrepancy checks; 33 unchanged focused records are retained, giving 64 focused recorded passes per modeC-200). Missing identities or nonfinite values invalidate the collection. No averaging, favorable-backend selection, negative-flux clipping or physical mode assignment is performed. A flux-preserving conservative stable energy closure remains to be reviewed; a negative effective turbulent diffusivity does not by itself justify negative total diffusion. ## Reference repeatability {#reference-repeatability}
The bounded fresh-process diagnostic completes and its saved-output audit passes (521 saved-output checks pass; every within-backend fresh-process repeat is exactly equal and agrees with its consumed output, while all four cross-backend discrepancies persist; native accounting completes within the reviewed bound and the offline archive copy matches its checksumC-201). For each selected state, native and wrapper backends receive two unchanged-input calls. Report each species vector separately; compare the two vectors within a backend and compare each with that backend’s consumed result. Retain cross-backend comparisons separately at the existing mixed 1e-12 criterion.
Within-backend vectors repeat exactly; the prior cross-backend differences persist. Repeatability cannot establish numerical convergence or physical validity. The historical pinned wrapper remains the reproduction anchor, while the native output route supplies additional diagnostics. A read-only assignment audit finds no observable input-register precision loss. The cause of backend differences remains unresolved; no particular compilation or physical mechanism is asserted.
The next reference review should quantify basis/quadrature/wavenumber convergence with predeclared refinements and unchanged baseline controls. Any stable signed energy closure must retain the reviewed flux, conserve energy and demonstrate time/grid convergence. The served surrogate contract, raw guard and temperature threshold remain fixed. K-030 and M4 stay open.

title: Verification
text:
Bounded reference refinement
The synthetic refinement and evidence checks pass (40 focused synthetic checks pass in each mode after the input-path correction, covering signed channels, refinement identities, baseline drift, incomplete evidence and existing diagnostic output handlingC-202). Retain original settings, then vary parallel basis, Gauss–Hermite quadrature and high-wavenumber resolution separately and together. Both minimum and maximum basis settings vary, affecting width optimization and the final eigenvalue solve. Their effects are not isolated by that ladder. Pinned KYGRID_MODEL=4 leaves its low-wavenumber nodes fixed while NKY refines its logarithmic high-wavenumber part.
For each backend and species, report all fluxes, observed minimum/maximum, successive differences and sign changes. Form the ion sum before taking these statistics. Relative last-step differences divide by the larger absolute flux at the two levels, with zero/zero reported as zero. No flux floor, averaging, Richardson extrapolation or new acceptance threshold is introduced. Backend parity at the existing mixed tolerance remains separate from physical convergence.
The first execution failed before solver calls on relative historical evidence paths after a working-directory change. The path fix and relocated preflight preserve source/input bindings. A separate quota-failed preparation is retained; OQ-35 approves alternate shared-work storage for this diagnostic only. K-030, reference admissibility and coupled acceptance remain open pending measurements.

title: Verification
text:
Reference refinement result
The complete bounded collection passes its saved-output audit (2076 integrity checks pass on the complete bounded study; baseline reproduction, signed species outputs, spectral accounting, native completion and the local archive copy are verified, while electron-flux signs change across refinement levels and finest-level backend differences remainC-203), but the reference remains numerically unconverged. Signed electron heat changes sign across levels at every selected state in both backends. The joint minimum-/maximum-basis ladder has substantially greater sensitivity than the separate quadrature and high-ky ladders. Since minimum basis sets the width-search calculation and maximum basis sets the final solve, the current evidence cannot assign the effect to one component. Finest-level backend differences persist. No particular compiler or physical instability is identified.
Next separate those two basis roles and retain width/growth diagnostics before extending the refinement budget. Low-ky, width-search resolution and mode-count limits remain explicit. A stable conservative signed-energy closure remains a later conditional review, not a consequence of seeing negative values at the finest tested resolution. Current model/guard, the temperature criterion and K-030 remain unchanged; no new coupled acceptance is evaluated.
The archive is checksum-matched in the authoritative local tracking record. Simvue’s mirror was unavailable; neither a remote record nor an upload is claimed.

title: Verification
text:
Separate basis roles
The factorial diagnostic crosses width-search basis and final-solve basis while holding other saved settings fixed. Its synthetic reporting checks pass (54 focused synthetic checks pass in each mode, including separated basis effects, interactions, signed channels, incomplete evidence and consumed-control drift; 553 unchanged recorded checks are retained separatelyC-204). Report changes along each fixed-other-basis axis and the cross-difference relative to the original minimum/maximum setting; retain signs, species channels, total-ion sums and both backends. Prior diagonal cells serve as reproduction controls, not convergence targets.
The native output driver reads selected width, saved search growth and retained final-mode spectra from the unchanged linked library. The protocol requires zero shear and a fresh width search: the double-pass path could overwrite a register with a different meaning. The retained width can revert to its input value if the final solve finds no unstable mode. Mode ranks are not tracked physical branches. The wrapper supplies fluxes only. Freeze and verify the package before the bounded allocation, then reconstruct its saved outputs independently.

Basis-role results
The completed grid passes its saved-output audit and reproduces all consumed controls (2139 integrity checks pass on the complete 54-pair basis grid and all 36 consumed-control comparisons reproduce the preceding study; electron flux changes sign at every state, steps reach 4.28 gB along the final basis and 4.11 gB along the search basis, and at the largest final basis the flux is a residual of order 1e-3 gBC-205). Both roles change the flux: steps along the final-solve basis are typically larger, but single steps along the search basis also exceed 4 gB, and cross-differences reach 3.96 gB. Search growth is identical across final-basis settings, and every width change along the final basis is the stable-solve fallback to the input width. At the largest final basis, low-ky flux collapses and the remaining signed flux is of order 1e-3 gB; at the middle final basis with larger search basis, high-ky roots with growth rates of 2-4 carry much of the flux. Up to half of unstable cells select the upper width bound. These are register observations; they identify no physical branch, cause or correct setting.


Extension results
The extension diagnostic passes its audit and reproduces its controls (3029 integrity checks pass on the complete 78-pair extension and all 36 control comparisons reproduce job 2687308; NBASIS_MAX 16 still moves electron flux by up to 0.48 gB per step, and widening the width search from 1.65 to 3.3 changes it from about 1e-3 gB to as much as 181 gBC-206). Raising the final basis from 10 to 16 does not settle the electron flux, and high-ky electron-direction roots appear and vanish along the ladder. Raising the width search’s upper bound from 1.65 to 2.3 and 3.3 changes the flux by up to five orders of magnitude, almost entirely at ky≤1; the default bound is selected often, and the search optimum becomes interior only at 3.3 for the standard basis. These are observations of the pinned solver, not error bounds or causes. The standard settings remain the training-label convention (K-032).

title: JOREK
text: JOREK is a nonlinear extended-MHD code with a flux-aligned finite-element grid that includes the X-point, scrape-off layer and divertor. The Tokamak Toolkit uses it as an external, open (Tier A) reference for MHD stability, which its transport loop does not model. It serves brief invariants 1–3: JOREK runs outside JAX, is never called inside compiled code, and is never a runtime dependency of a surrogate.

title: JOREK
text:
Build
JOREK is built from source at a pinned commit; there are no tagged releases. The build uses GNU Fortran 12.3 and OpenMPI 4.1 with OpenBLAS, ScaLAPACK, FFTW, HDF5, METIS and ParMETIS. The sparse direct solver is our own MUMPS 5.7.3 build, with PORD, METIS and ParMETIS orderings. Binaries are compiled for x86-64-v3, so the same binary runs on the Intel login nodes and the AMD compute nodes. util/config.sh fixes the physics model and toroidal resolution at compile time and edits a source file, so each configuration is built in its own git worktree.






Build notes






MUMPS: build the real and complex libraries one after the other. A parallel build of both races on Fortran module files.
GNU Fortran rejects a space between a namelist name and its subscript (name (1) = …), which Intel Fortran accepts. Upstream inputs are rewritten without it; values are unchanged.
The code’s default solver is STRUMPACK. Runs with MUMPS set use_mumps = .t. and use_strumpack = .f. in the namelist.
eqdsk2jorek needs the DIERCKX (FITPACK) spline library, built from netlib with double-precision default reals.
With more than one toroidal harmonic, JOREK needs at least two MPI ranks.




Regression checks. These use JOREK’s own cases and the reference data the JOREK team publishes, so the check does not depend on toolkit code (3 of 4 upstream regression cases reproduce their public reference data: MAST-U grid and equilibrium (largest difference 2.0e-5, tolerance 1e-4), MAST equilibrium with coils (1.2e-10), and one implicit tearing-mode step (4.1e-13, tolerance 1e-12); the full-MHD kink case was not run because its upstream input is out of date for this code versionC-210). On the compute nodes, one job repeated them and measured the step cost (all three regression cases pass on a 256-core AMD node; one implicit step on the MAST-U X-point grid (8050 elements, toroidal modes n = 0 and 1) takes 5.8 s at 2 ranks x 16 threads, 6.7 s at 4 x 32 and 8.1 s at 2 x 64; the whole job used 22.4 core-hoursC-211).

title: JOREK
text:
Unit conversion and input files
tkit.adapters.jorek (Tier A, host side) converts between SI/eV and JOREK’s normalised units. With \(n_0 = \texttt{central\_density}\cdot10^{20}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\) and \(\rho_0 = \texttt{central\_mass}\cdot m_\mathrm{u}\, n_0\):
\[
n = \rho\, n_0,\qquad T_\mathrm{eV} = \frac{T}{e\,\mu_0\, n_0},\qquad
t_\mathrm{SI} = t\,\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0},\qquad \gamma_\mathrm{SI} = \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_0}},
\]
using the constants of the pinned JOREK version (models/constants.f90), not CODATA. Single-temperature models evolve \(T = T_e + T_i\), with \(p = \rho T/\mu_0\). The toroidal mode number of Fourier component \(k\) (1-based) is \(\lfloor k/2\rfloor\, n_\mathrm{period}\).
What the adapter covers:

Profile files are two bare numeric columns (\(\psi_N\), value). JOREK’s reader stops silently at the first unparseable line, so the writer emits no header and reads every file back for an exact match.
Namelists are written one entry per line, with full precision and no space before subscripts. Index ranges such as fbnd(2:4) and both quote styles are supported. A parser for JOREK inputs is included.
Energy reader. It reads magnetic and kinetic energy per Fourier component from a restart file, and checks the array shapes and that the stored time unit matches the normalisation.
Growth rates are a least-squares fit of \(\tfrac12\ln E\) against time over a window the caller must give. No default window is offered, because choosing the linear phase is part of the analysis.

Correctness. - The conversion matches the units JOREK stored in three restart files (time and resistivity units computed by the toolkit match the values JOREK stored in three restart files to 1e-15 relativeC-213). - A rewritten MAST-U input gives an identical restart file (the MAST-U input (356 entries) parsed and rewritten by the toolkit gives, with one thread, a restart file identical in every dataset to a run of the original inputC-214). - The tests are in 26 tests pass in normal and Tier-A-only modes: unit conversion, profile files, namelists, the energy reader, and the runner with fake executables (snapshots, retry, timeout, provenance)C-215.
Design decisions. - Conversion only, deliberately. JOREK’s own scripts hard-code physics choices: the scrape-off-layer extension, diffusivities, resistivity and grid sizes. Here each of them is a required input, so it reaches the owner as a decision (OQ-39). - Native HDF5, not IMAS output. JOREK’s IDS writer needs the IMAS Fortran access layer, and its Python scripts use the pre-2.0 IMAS API.

title: JOREK
text:
Run wrapper
tkit.datasets.jorek_run runs one case in a new directory:

It snapshots the executable and every input read-only, and verifies any input provenance.
Each attempt gets fresh working copies. The namelist goes on standard input, and the launcher sets MPI ranks and OpenMP threads explicitly.
The process group is killed at the timeout, and partial output is kept.
The outcome is classified: completed, solver aborted, grid set-up abort, JOREK error, non-zero exit or timeout.
A provenance record is written beside every retained file. result.json records ranks, threads and whether the run is bitwise repeatable.

Two measured JOREK properties shape it (an assertion in the element search tree aborts 3 of 8 grid set-up runs at 8 OpenMP threads and 0 of 8 at 1 thread; two 4-thread runs of the same input differ at round-off, while 1-thread runs repeat bit for bitC-212): - Threaded runs are not bitwise repeatable, so only one-thread runs are marked repeatable. - Threaded runs intermittently abort on an assertion in the element search tree during grid set-up, before any time step. The wrapper retries only that case, only before the first step, and keeps every attempt.
On the real program the wrapper reproduces a manual run exactly. A completed run is not physical acceptance.






Post-mortem: a GMRES abort recorded as a completed run (2026-10-24)






What was written, and what was correct. The wrapper classified any run that exited with code 0 as completed, unless it had timed out or hit the known grid set-up assertion. JOREK stops a run whose iterative linear solver (GMRES) fails to converge, but it exits with code 0. The correct classification is a separate outcome, solver_aborted: the energies up to the abort are valid data, and the run is not retried, because a retry would fail the same way.
What it looked like from inside. All eight linear runs of the first case (a) scan ended this way and were recorded as completed (8 of 8 case (a) runs ended on the GMRES abort with exit code 0; a test now checks that such a run is recorded as solver_aborted and not retriedC-230). Every wrapper check passed: the exit code was 0, the output files existed, and the provenance records were complete. None of them reads the end of the log.
What caught it. The growth-rate analysis: the energy traces ended at different times, and each run’s log ended with the abort message. The analysis reads JOREK’s own output, not the wrapper’s status, so it is independent of the classifier.
Before and after. Before: 8 of 8 runs completed. After: 8 of 8 solver_aborted, energies kept.
What changed. The abort string is now an outcome of its own. The test test_gmres_abort_with_exit_zero_is_not_completed runs a stub JOREK that prints the abort and exits 0, and checks that the run is classified solver_aborted and is not retried.
Blast radius. None published: no growth rate had been reported from these runs. The abort follows the linear phase in every run, so the growth data stay usable.

text:
ITER hybrid equilibrium
Input: the ITER hybrid EQDSK distributed with TORAX (COCOS 2, \(I_p\) 11.77 MA, \(B_0\) 5.3 T). A JOREK stability run starts from an equilibrium JOREK solves itself, from a boundary, a pressure profile and FF′. The acceptance tolerance (OQ-39, decision 2) is q within 2% of the source over \(\psi_N\) 0.1–0.95, and \(I_p\) within 1%, before any stability run.
Current route: fixed boundary on the EQDSK separatrix. The boundary is the EQDSK separatrix itself: 300 points on the flux surface \(\psi = \psi_\mathrm{bnd}\), ordered by angle about the geometric centre, with no X-point and a polar flux-aligned grid (scripts/jorek/iter_lcfs_input.py). Pressure and FF′ are those of the first route below. JOREK model303 solves the fixed-boundary equilibrium on one core.

The largest q difference, 1.1%, is in the core and is the same on all three grids. Edge q agrees to better than 0.3%. The current deficit shrinks with resolution but is not yet in a clean asymptotic regime. The 80 × 128 grid is used for the n-scans and 160 × 256 for the doubled-resolution check.
Limitation. A fixed boundary at the separatrix acts as an ideal conducting wall there, with no vacuum region. Peeling modes, which need one, are artificially stabilised. All growth rates on this page carry this limitation.
First route: eqdsk2jorek (2026-10-16). eqdsk2jorek produced the boundary, FF′ and namelist after three changes: - the spline smoothing was raised from 1e-6 to 3e-5, the smallest value for which the fit succeeds; the RMS fit error is about 2e-7 Wb; - the converter’s pressure continuation went to −10 Pa outside the separatrix, because the EQDSK pressure there is 0 and the converter’s edge value is 10 Pa; - the temperature file was therefore written by the toolkit: EQDSK pressure inside, a 10 Pa floor outside, check-only.
Its result, JOREK solving the ITER hybrid equilibrium from the TORAX EQDSK matches its safety factor q to 0.4% (median) for normalised flux 0.1-0.5, but is 3.6% high for 0.5-0.9 and 5.8% high for 0.9-0.95 (q 5.12 vs 4.67 at 0.95); plasma current 12.06 vs 11.77 MAC-216 (superseded by C-221), failed the tolerance at the edge.






Post-mortem: the edge mismatch came from the converter’s boundary (2026-10-16)






What was written, and what was correct. eqdsk2jorek builds a free-boundary-style domain from a default ITER contour outside the wall, and takes ψ on that contour from the EQDSK. That is correct only if the EQDSK grid covers the contour. The TORAX EQDSK comes from a fixed-boundary CHEASE solve: its R–Z grid holds no X-point (\(|\nabla\psi|\) has no zero inside it, and a minimiser leaves the grid), and 187 of the contour’s 257 points lay outside the grid. ψ there was extrapolated, and JOREK built its own X-point and separatrix, enclosing a larger plasma than the EQDSK’s. The correct boundary for this source is its own separatrix.
What it looked like from inside. The converter ran without error once the smoothing was raised, the sign conventions all came out right, and core q matched to 0.4%. Only edge q and the current were off, by a few percent, which entry 65 listed with three candidate causes.
What caught it. Checking where the contour points fall relative to the EQDSK grid, then solving on the separatrix, which removes the edge mismatch at every resolution.

Each job runs an axisymmetric start, then a health gate, then all n in parallel from that state. The gate requires the minimum of ψ within 1e-3 (relative) of the equilibrium’s axis value, since a deeper minimum signals a blow-up, and positive density and temperature. Two keys that JOREK’s own IMAS input script sets (eta_coul_log_dep, T_min_ZKpar) don’t exist in model303 and are left out.
Growth-rate analysis (scripts/jorek/j5_growth.py). γ is the least-squares slope of ½ ln E of the total (magnetic + kinetic) energy over an energy band. A phase counts as linear only if the two half-windows and the separate magnetic and kinetic fits agree within 2%, over at least 20 points. The band, 1e-15 to 1e-7, was chosen after inspecting the case (a) traces; the first rule, a steady per-step rate over the final segment, cannot work when every run ends in a solver abort and some modes exchange energy between the magnetic and kinetic parts every few steps. Location is the peak of the RMS perturbation over \(\psi_N\) bins: axis if the peak is below 0.05, edge at or above 0.8, otherwise core. Since case (b), it is reported from both the temperature (class) and the flow perturbation (class_u). ωᵢ and γ/ω are estimates computed from the profiles, not JOREK outputs.


Case (a): the EQDSK as given
Pressure from the EQDSK, split into density and temperature with TORAX’s main-ion density at 80 s (D-T, mean mass 2.515 amu). The total axis temperature is therefore high (66.6 keV in case (a) (EQDSK pressure split by TORAX density) against 14.4 keV in case (b) (TORAX at 80 s)C-239): the EQDSK is a higher-pressure state than TORAX at that time, and diamagnetic stabilisation is overstated.

Job 1 (Δt = 3) was lost: its axisymmetric start went numerically unstable, and every linear run failed on its first step. The health gate was added after it.
Job 2 (Δt = 1) ran 3 h 51 min. Every linear run grew from about 1e-20 over roughly 16 decades and then stopped on JOREK’s GMRES abort (8 of 8 case (a) runs ended on the GMRES abort with exit code 0; a test now checks that such a run is recorded as solver_aborted and not retriedC-230). In this JOREK version linear_run is keep_n0_const: n = 0 is frozen, but the n ≠ 0 equations stay nonlinear, so the matrix drifts as the mode grows and the GMRES iteration count rises step by step until it fails. The doubled grid never got past its axisymmetric start (about 126 s per step against 9.7 s on 80 x 128 (13x); timed out after 43 of 50 steps, so no doubled-grid linear run startedC-229). Scaling the step cost by the same factor gives roughly 50–75 s per linear step; the n = 12 and 16 fit windows need about 700–800 steps, so about 10–17 h at 32 cores. These are estimates, not measurements; either way a linear run on this grid needs more than one 6 h job.
The job also lost compute to a batch-script bug (about 290 of 1046 core-h: after the last run ended the script waited on its watchdog (an empty wait list became a bare wait); fixed in both job scriptsC-232). The script waited on its background jobs other than the watchdog, wait $(jobs -p | grep -v …). When that list was empty, the command became a bare wait, which also waits for the watchdog, and the watchdog never exits. Both J5 job scripts now skip the wait when the list is empty.
Decision OQ-41. Case (a) is closed on the Δt check: n = 12 and 16 are “converged in Δt, grid not checked”, not quotable; the other six n are “not measured: core or axis mode faster”. The full check moves to case (b), with up to five one-node jobs of ≤ 6 h, each announced.


Case (b) equilibrium
Case (b) is the TORAX ITER hybrid state at 80 s: pressure from TORAX’s density and temperatures, FF′ from TORAX’s current density with the bootstrap current. The FF′ formula reproduces the EQDSK’s own FF′ from the CHEASE geometry to 2.4%.
The first solve gave \(I_p\) +3.7% (10.89 against 10.5 MA) and q +7.8% (median, \(\psi_N\) 0.1–0.5), outside decision 2. The cause is structural: TORAX evolves the current on a fixed CHEASE geometry, so its state is not a Grad–Shafranov equilibrium, and a consistent equilibrium with the same p and j has different flux surfaces and q.
Decision OQ-40 (a). FF′ is multiplied by one factor k so that \(I_p\) = 10.5 MA. Acceptance: \(I_p\) within 1%, and p(\(\psi_N\)) as TORAX’s by construction. The q difference from TORAX is reported as a known inconsistency of the fixed-geometry TORAX state. Rejected: (b) tuning FF′ until q matches, which moves the current profile away from TORAX’s; (c) a self-consistent free-boundary TORAX state first, a larger piece of work.
Convergence of the Grad–Shafranov iteration. Without under-relaxation every case (b) solve stalls (the iteration cycles between two states for all 200 iterations (axis moves about 5 mm, residual about 7e-3); I_p +3.7% at FF’ x 1, −0.0002% at x 0.952, neither convergedC-234): the magnetic axis moves between R 6.2986 and 6.3038 m on alternate iterations. The 2026-10-16 solve already had this (residual 8.2e-3) and it was not flagged then. Case (b)’s FF′ is hollow, because the ramp-up current has not yet reached the core, so the axis is weakly pinned. JOREK’s amix 0.5 (\(\psi_\mathrm{new}\) = 0.5 \(\psi_\mathrm{old}\) + 0.5 \(\psi_\mathrm{solve}\)) converges it to 1e-6 in 43 iterations.
